To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the energy efficiency of the air transport sector has improved in the last 20 years and that this improvement is not the same for all geographical regions.

the energy efficiency of air transport has increased by 2.88%/year between 1983 and 2006, that the energy efficiency coefficients differ from region to region and that domestic air travels have a larger energy intensity than international air travels.

the energy efficiency of air transport varies significantly from one region to another, and that the energy efficiency coefficient of domestic air transport is systematically lower than that of international air transport.
In summary, our research is concerned with
energy efficiency coefficients and the evolution of energy efficiency in air transport at the world level and for eight geographical regions.
the macro-level energy efficiency of air travel and the evolution of energy efficiency coefficients and energy gains.
the energy efficiency evolution in the air transportation sector, and it contributes to the debate about the energy performance of air transport.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the energy efficiency gains of the air transport industry have been higher than the energy efficiency gains in other transport modes, but not high enough to offset its strong growth in demand.
the air transport sector is a major contributor to global warming, and its energy efficiency is not increasing as much as expected.
air transport is not an energy efficient sector and that its efficiency has not improved much in the last 20 years.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
air traffic energy efficiency is not the same in every region and that domestic flights are more energy intensive than international flights.
air traffic energy efficiency differs between regions and that domestic air travels tend to be more energy inefficient than international air travels.
air transport energy efficiency differs from region to region and that domestic air travels tend to be less energy efficient than international air travels, regardless of the region.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the energy efficiency of the air transport sector is a function of the geographical region where it takes place.
the air transport sector has been able to improve energy efficiency at a rate that is higher than the rate of growth of its energy demand.

the air transport sector should not be treated as a homogeneous entity, and that energy efficiency gains should be analysed from a regional point of view, in particular in the context of international negotiations.
